## Product-record interface

Let one already-classical X persist through r>=1 iid cheap records with a
known finite rational channel L. Set W=(Z1,...,Zr) and define the rational
column-stochastic channel M_{w,x}=product_i L_{z_i,x}. Conditional independence
and persistence give this law for every x;column sums are (sum_z L_zx)^r=1.
A single M record is an actually acquired r-record block,not one free L call.
It requires r conditional draws,delayed output,storage/streaming and decoding.

Apply N1073's general rational subchannel LP to supplied target K and channel M.
For any U>=0 with column sums<=1 and UM<=K,the no-raw branch has mass UM and
the known queried residual has mass D=K-UM. The raw branch probability is
q_x=sum_y D_yx,and its post-read output D_.x/q_x completes exactly K at every x.
Conversely,any protocol that sees the whole acquired block before optional raw
access has a no-raw table U_{y,w} independent of x,so the same LP is complete
for that interface. Adaptive early stopping within a hard r budget may be padded
by unused iid draws;the U table can average them away. This does not establish
an optimum among arbitrary unbounded-stopping/calibration-unknown protocols.

There are k^r ordered records for a k-letter proxy. Type compression is available
for an iid exchangeable decoder only with its exact multinomial law;it is not
a free reduction for an arbitrary correlated or state-changing source. Explicit
LP/certificate input/output size and bit arithmetic grow with the chosen record
representation. The old generic simplex backend is not newly audited here.

## Exact two-call specialization

For the acquired source K,L,let c be the number of zeros in two actual iid
records. A no-read output-zero probability w_c=(13/25,17/100,0) gives

 sum_{z1,z2} L_{z1,x}L_{z2,x} w_c
   =13/25-(7/10)p_x+(9/50)p_x^2,
 p_x=L_{0,x}.

At p0=2/3 this is2/15;at p1=p2=1/6 it is49/120. Splitting the remaining mass
equally produces the complete K column. The U table is stochastic,so this is
an exact zero-raw feasible certificate for the product-record LP. It does not
contradict the prior one-L-record optimum3/40:the acquired record and cheap-call
budget changed. Ordinary classifier/confusion inversion in the supplied extension
also achieves two cheap calls with no raw,so no special advantage is established.

## One-step construction and completeness

Let U be an m-by-k nonnegative matrix. Put s_z=sum_y U_yz and require

    s_z <= 1,             U L <= K entrywise.                         (1)

Define r_z=1-s_z, D=K-U L and

    q_x = 1-sum_z L_zx s_z = sum_y D_yx.                              (2)

Given z, choose outcome y without a raw read with probability U_yz for each y;
with the remaining probability r_z, request X. If the raw value is x, choose y
with probability D_yx/q_x. Ignore z on this queried branch. If q_x=0, the
queried branch has zero probability for that x; choose its unused rule
arbitrarily. This uses valid distributions because D>=0 and (2) holds.
For each x,y, its total output probability is exactly

    sum_z L_zx U_yz + sum_z L_zx r_z D_yx/q_x
       = (UL)_yx + D_yx = K_yx.                                     (3)

The no-read/query decision is made without knowing X. The code's raw callback
is only invoked on a query branch.

Conversely, fix a private pre-round history of any permitted one-step protocol.
Before its first raw request, it has only Z and X-independent private
randomness. Therefore

    U_yz = Pr[no raw request and output y | record z]

is independent of x. Its columns have mass at most one. The probability of
output y on the no-read branch at input x is (UL)_yx; exactness forces this to
be at most K_yx. Its raw-read probability is exactly (2). Its post-query output
rule can depend on x and z, but (3) replaces it with a rule depending only on x,
without changing either the output channel or raw-read probabilities. Repeated
reads of the same current classical symbol can be cached. Thus (1) describes
all one-step possibilities in the declared resource contract.

Consequently the exact acquisition problem is the rational LP

    minimize q
    U>=0, q>=0,
    sum_y U_yz <= 1                              for each z,
    sum_z U_yz L_zx <= K_yx                      for each y,x,
    1-sum_z L_zx sum_y U_yz <= q                 for each x.          (P)

U=0,q=1 is feasible, so 0<=q*<=1. U is in a compact product of substochastic
simplices; restricting q to [0,1] changes no optimum. A rational optimum exists.

q*=0 exactly when K is a stochastic postprocessing of L. Indeed D>=0 and
zero column masses force D=0. Every record z reachable at some x then has
s_z=1; unused z columns can be completed arbitrarily to a stochastic matrix.
